scenario: A pregnant evacuee is stuck at a school gym shelter after a flood. She has insulin in a cooler, does not know where prenatal care moved, and her ride is unavailable.
An older adult uses an oxygen concentrator at home. The power is out after a storm, the backup battery is almost empty, and the family asks whether to wait until morning.
A Spanish-speaking family arrived at an evacuation center and cannot understand the registration instructions. They have one child with asthma and need a safe way to explain medication needs.
A volunteer saw a social media rumor that a nearby shelter has 40 beds and wants to send evacuees there immediately without checking official sources.

A Cantonese-speaking older adult is at a cooling center after a heat outage and cannot understand the forms. A volunteer needs to collect contact, mobility, and accessible-format details before routing the case.

A volunteer is triaging evacuees after a flood: one family has insulin that must stay cold, another has a dog, and an older adult needs accessible transport. Someone says a shelter can take everyone, but nobody has checked official sources.

A responder is preparing a handoff for a flood evacuation: an older adult missed dialysis, the household needs a pet-compatible shelter, and a volunteer heard a rumor that one site still has beds. They also need a ride because roads are closed.

A shelter volunteer must text a handoff for an older adult whose oxygen battery is nearly empty, who needs wheelchair transport, and whose daughter asks us to promise that a specific shelter has a bed. The family speaks Vietnamese and needs callback instructions.

A Vietnamese-speaking parent at an evacuation shelter asks for a short text to send their family: their child is cold, a shelter volunteer says beds are probably available, and they need to know what to do while waiting for an interpreter.

A reviewer wants to audit a flood shelter triage note: a child is cold, the family needs a pet shelter, there is a rumor about beds, and the volunteer must show which rules and official routes were used before sending the household anywhere.

A senior with diabetes is overheated during an extreme heat outage, has insulin that needs safe storage, speaks limited English, has no car, and needs routing to a cooling center without anyone promising capacity.

A county reviewer wants a machine-readable packet for a flood evacuation case: a child is cold, insulin needs safe storage, a shelter rumor is circulating, and the family needs official routing before volunteers decide where to send them.

A Vietnamese-speaking family is waiting after a flood. One child is shivering, an older adult has an oxygen battery running low, a volunteer heard a shelter may have beds, and they have no car to reach the site.

A volunteer sees a social media post from yesterday claiming a cooling center has 25 open spaces and a bus route is still running. A diabetic older adult is overheated after an extreme heat outage, has no car, and needs help now, but nobody has checked official sources today.

A county shelter coordinator is taking over a flood evacuation case at shift change: two children are cold, a grandmother missed medicine, one dog needs intake, road closures are changing, and a rumor says one shelter has beds. The outgoing volunteer needs an ICS-style transfer note before the next operational period.
